title: Activation matrix & safety heuristics — lab notes
summary: Working notes that propose an activation matrix (multi-dimensional exposure control) and a set of lightweight safety heuristics for feature exposure and A/B experiments. Oriented toward cross-functional coordination: product, eng, SRE, and CS. This is an operational draft — contains simulation outputs, gating rules, and monitoring playbook fragments.
context: Why this exists: we repeatedly hit ambiguous decisions during staged feature exposure (fast ramp vs conservative safety) and the team wants a compact decision surface that maps risk vectors to exposure steps. Goal: a concise matrix + heuristics that teams can apply without a full runbook for every small change.
activation-matrix:
Overview:
- Dimensions: user_impact (low|medium|high), data_sensitivity (public|internal|restricted), latency_criticality (yes|no), traffic_variability (stable|spiky).
- Each cell maps to a default exposure pattern: (seed -> micro -> regional -> global) and default monitoring cadence.
Example row (high user_impact, restricted, latency_critical): seed=0.05% internal-only -> micro=0.5% with feature-flag ramp -> regional=5% with synchronous tracing -> global=gradual pinned rollout with tiered fallback.
Decision notes: use the matrix as a starting point. If product/eng/SRE jointly score any dimension as "one step higher" due to uncertainty, escalate to the activation council (Slack @activation-oncall).
How to use in planning doc: include matrix cell id (e.g., H-R-L) in PR template. The release pipeline should interpret that id and suggest default feature flag parameters and monitoring queries.
safety-heuristics:
Core heuristics (keep short and memorizable):
1) Smoke-before-expose: run a synthetic smoke test in staging that exercises the critical path with realistic KV cache sizes. Only pass traffic if smoke is green for 30m.
2) Circuit-window: if error-rate increases by >2x baseline OR absolute p50 latency worsens by >200ms over a 15m sliding window, divert new traffic for 30m and notify owners.
3) Prefix-fallthrough: for new generation models, enable a fallback variant that matches tokenization/formatting differences within first 500 tokens.
4) Cost-sentinel: if per-request token-cost exceeds baseline by >30% for a cohort, pause non-critical cohorts and notify finance-algorithms.
5) Data-sensitivity lock: any change touching restricted-data paths requires an HADR (high-assurance) sign-off before regional exposure.
Notes: heuristics are intentionally conservative; they can be relaxed for mature features with historical stability. All heuristics map to concrete alert thresholds in the monitoring playbook section.
monitoring-playbook:
Minimum dashboards/alerts to wire up (template links in linked_artifacts):
- Slice-level: latency p50/p95, error-rate, token-rate, cost-per-req (1m and 15m windows). Alert if thresholds crossed for 5m.
- Health traces: single-request flamegraphs sampled at 1% traffic for new slices.
- Behavioral signal: semantic similarity drift (e.g., embedding drift >0.2 avg) for generation features.
- Business signal: key downstream conversions by cohort (A/B conversion delta, 95% CI).
Escalation path: paging to SRE primary -> product PM -> eng oncall. Maintain a 2-hour SLA to acknowledge and 8-hour SLA to mitigate for high-impact slices.
Playbook snippets to copy into incident-run template: what changed, who approved exposure, slice id, traffic fraction, rollback steps, fallback model id.
rollforward-rollback-criteria:
Rollback (fast): immediately revert if any of these within 30 minutes of exposure increase:
- User-facing errors increase >3x baseline and absolute increase >0.5%
- p95 latency increases by >500ms
- Cost-per-req increases >50% and trending
Rollforward (fast): allow step-up if sustained 60m with no alerts and business metrics steady.
Rollforward (manual): product can request manual increase if qualitative user feedback from CS is positive and no alerts in 48h.
Documentation requirement: every rollforward must include a short justification in the release PR and a CI artifact proving smoke tests and traffic replay results.
simulated-slices-and-cohorts:
We ran quick local simulations (see linked GitHub) with two knobs: burstiness and model-latency amplification. Key takeaways:
- Small micro slices (<=0.5% traffic) have high variance; prefer longer observation windows (60-120m) before second step.
- Regional exposure reduces overall correlation between errors and global user impact by ~60% in our sim if regions are orthogonal in backend dependency.
- For latency-sensitive features, parallel canary (same user served by both legacy and new path) reduces false positives in p95 latency checks.
Recommended default cohort sets: Seed (internal staff + 0.01%), Micro (1% stratified by geo + device), Regional (5% by region), Public (gradual up to 100%).
Practical note: avoid tiny slices across too many regions simultaneously (operational churn). Consolidate early phases into 1–2 regions only.
open-questions:
- Should activation_matrix be encoded as structured metadata in the release pipeline (yes) and which system owns scoring? (suggestion: product assigns initial score, SRE verifies).
- How to standardize 'business-signal' thresholds across PMs? propose a lightweight checklist (conversion uplift targets, user-sentiment proxies) to be adopted.
- Ownership of cost-sentinel alerts: pass-through to finance vs keep within infra? (preference: infra owns immediate mitigation, finance notified).
- Do we require legal review for features flagged as 'restricted' every time the model architecture changes? (TBD with security/compliance).
